examples.text: С ним случилось в эту минуту то, что случается с людьми, когда они неожиданно уличены в чём-нибудь слишком постыдном.

glosses: то же, что спариваться
To occur or take place.

examples.text: Let me tell you how it happened.
Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic who still resists the idea that something drastic needs to happen for him to turn his life around.

glosses: To happen to; to befall.

examples.text: 'By my soul! I believe something bad has happened me,' he muttered, and popped up his window, and looked out, half dreaming over the church-yard on the park beyond […]

glosses: To do or occur by chance or unexpectedly.

examples.text: Take an umbrella in case it happens to rain.
Do you happen to have an umbrella?
If you should (happen to) need any help, I'll be there.

glosses: To encounter by chance.

examples.text: Unexpectedly, in a nook close by the farmhouse, he happened upon a spot where the vintage had actually commenced.

glosses: To become popular or trendy.
maybe, perhaps.

examples.text: Yeah, well happen if he'd gone quietly, she wouldn't have needed to show him who's in charge.

glosses: Destiny, especially favorable.

examples.text: She read my fortune. Apparently I will have a good love life this week, but I will have a bad week for money.
you, who men's fortunes in their faces read
[…]his lordship was out of humour. That was the way Chollacombe described as knaggy an old gager as ever Charles had had the ill-fortune to serve.

glosses: A prediction or set of predictions about a person's future provided by a fortune teller.
A small slip of paper with wise or vaguely prophetic words printed on it, baked into a fortune cookie.
The arrival of something in a sudden or unexpected manner; chance; accident.

examples.text: 'Tis more by fortune, lady, than by merit.

glosses: Good luck.

examples.text: fame and fortune
Fortune favors the brave.
There is a tide in the affairs of men / Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune.

glosses: One's wealth; the amount of money one has, especially if it is vast.

examples.text: He's amassed a small fortune working in the Middle East.
My vast fortune was a result of inheritance and stock market nous.
Her fortune is estimated at 3 million dollars.
It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.

glosses: A large amount of money.

examples.text: That car must be worth a fortune! How could you afford it?

Why spend a small fortune on Puma when you could buy Numa, Tuna or Pigg? And why buy Adidas when you can buy Adidos or Avivas? Nike, when there's Nire or Hike? Calvin Klein, when clearly, Calvim Klain or Cavern Kernel are just as good? But remember, after a good workout, be sure to clean up with some Okay shampoo.

glosses: To provide (someone) with a fortune.
To tell the fortune of (someone); to presage.
To happen, to take place.

examples.text: Thẽ the heerdmẽ⸝ fleed and went there ways into the cite⸝ and tolde every thinge⸝ and what had fortuned vnto them that were poſſeſſed of the devyls.
It fortuned one night that the Sultan purposed setting out on a journey next morning, […]

glosses: Synonym of falling out (“rift following a disagreement or quarrel”).

examples.text: We had a fall out, couldn't come to terms and haven't talked since.
I've had a fall out with Nora, one of my tenants. She's packing up and leaving at this very moment.

glosses: To come out of something by falling.

examples.text: I opened the cupboard and a can fell out onto my foot.

Part of No. 10 platform at Kings Cross was cordoned off on August 23 after a container of radio-active material had fallen from a trolley. The special box in which it was packed split open, allowing the container to fall out.

glosses: To cease to be on friendly terms.

examples.text: Dave and I fell out after a long argument.

Petronius calleth this paſſion [i.e., jealousy] amantium furioſam æmulationem, a furious emulation, and their ſymptomes are well expreſſed by Sʳ Ieffrey Chaucer in his firſt Canterbury tale. It will make the neareſt & deareſt friends fall out; they will endure al other things to be common, goods, lands, moneyes, participate of all other pleaſures, and take in good part any diſgraces, iniuries in another kind, but as Propertius well deſcribes it in an Elegie of his, in this they will ſuffer nothing, have no corriuals.
Before the incident Robins had fallen out with Knutton, 30. Knutton had made a complaint over Robins' boyfriend.

glosses: To leave one's place in the current formation of ranks in order to take one's place in a new formation.
To leave one's current location to report for duty at a new location.

examples.text: The company fell out for an artillery drill.

glosses: To pass out.
To turn out, happen.

examples.text: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.
I expected to be in the States long before this, but things fell out otherwise.
For days Ailie had an absent eye and a sad face, and it so fell out that in all that time young Heriotside, who had scarce missed a day, was laid up with a broken arm and never came near her.

glosses: To fall off due to the quoins holding it in place having become wet and therefore loose.
To give way under someone.

examples.text: The board he was walking on fell out.

glosses: To cause someone to slip and/or fall down.

examples.text: When she left him, his world fell out beneath him.
The ground fell out from under him.

glosses: To be enthusiastic about something; to laugh very hard.

examples.text: When the band started, everybody fell out.

glosses: To depart.
To collapse; to pass out from intoxication.
To be shocked by something.
Entrar en lugar de otra persona en un cargo o situación.

examples.text: El nuevo presidente sucede al anterior en el cargo.

glosses: Entrar como heredero a poseer los bienes de un difunto.

examples.text: El marqués sucedió a su padre a la temprana edad de 5 años.

glosses: Descender, proceder, provenir.

examples.text: El pueblo que sucedió de Abraham es el pueblo de Israel.

glosses: Dicho de un hecho: ir tras otro, en orden.

examples.text: El sol sucede a la lluvia.

glosses: De un hecho: ocurrir.

examples.text: De lo que le sucedió a nuestro caballero cuando salió de la venta.

glosses: Aparecer algo sin una causa determinada, producirse espontáneamente.
Dicho de un evento o suceso, tener lugar, pasar o suceder.
Pedir la intercesión de un juez o autoridad.
Adelantarse a algo, reaccionar con anticipación.
Ir a un lugar.
Caer la fiesta de un santo en el mismo día de otra o de algún rito mayor.
avvenire per caso

glosses: widerfahren

examples.text: Mir ist etwas Schreckliches geschehen.
Mit ihm ist etwas Schreckliches geschehen.

examples.text: Wir haben soeben die Landesgrenze passiert.
„Alexei richtete sich nach dem Plan seiner Frau und passierte die Grenze ohne Probleme.“
„Es hat wohl Stunden gedauert, ehe sie es gewagt haben, unsern Rastort zu passieren und in die Felsenenge einzudringen.“
„Südirland war bei gutem Wind passiert worden.“

glosses: durchseihen (Flüssigkeiten), durchstreichen (weiche Nahrungsmittel, zum Beispiel um Schalenreste oder Kerne zu entfernen)

examples.text: Die Brühe durch ein feines Sieb passieren, die Flüssigkeit vorsichtig auffangen!
Auf der Speisekarte steht »Passierte Erbsensuppe mit Graupen«.

glosses: geschehen (ein Ereignis)

examples.text: Das darf nicht noch mal passieren!

examples.text: Komm doch mal vor zu mir!

examples.text: Auf der Insel kommen immer weniger Vogelarten vor.

glosses: jemandem passieren oder geschehen

examples.text: Es ist schon häufiger vorgekommen, dass Wörter falsch verwendet werden.

glosses: auf jemanden in einer Weise wirken

examples.text: Es kommt mir vor, als sei ich schon ewig hier.
